| Python Insider
# Python 3.15.0 candidate 3 is here!
...
Following recent tradition, here’s a surprise third release candidate for Python 3.15.0!
We got some last-minute lazy-import release blockers, and it makes sense to
include them in 3.15.0 final.
It also makes sense to give a bit of time to test
them properly, so this week’s planned 3.15.0 final is postponed until next week,
and here’s an extra 3.15.0rc3.
...
**This is a candidate preview of Python 3.15**
This release, **3.15.0rc3**, is the final planned release candidate, containing around 156 bugfixes, build improvements and documentation changes from 82 contributors since 3.15.0rc2.
Entering the release candidate phase, only reviewed code changes which are clear bug fixes are allowed between this release candidate and the final release.
The next release of Python 3.15 will be 3.15.0 final, scheduled for 2026-10-09.
There will be ***no ABI changes** * from this point forward in the 3.15 series, and the goal is that there will be as few code changes as possible.
...
# Call to action
We ***strongly encourage** * maintainers of third-party Python projects to prepare their projects for 3.15 during this phase, and publish Python 3.15 wheels on PyPI to be ready for the final release of 3.15.0, and to help other projects do their own testing.
Any binary wheels built against Python 3.15.0 release candidates ***will work** * with future versions of Python 3.15.
...
Please keep in mind that this is a preview release and while it’s as close to the final release as we can get it, its use is ***not** * recommended for production environments.
...
## Major new features of the 3.15 series, compared to 3.14
### Interpreter improvements
- PEP 810: Explicit lazy imports for faster startup times
...
### Build changes
...
### Release changes
- The official Windows 64-bit binaries now use the tail-calling interpreter
- The official macOS binaries now install free-threading support by default

Python 3.15.0 Is Out: Lazy Imports, frozendict, and Faster Speeds
...
## Python 3.15.0 Is Out: Lazy Imports, frozendict, and Faster Speeds
The final version of Python 3.15.0 has been released today, following a 17-month development cycle that produced 5,643 commits from 1,012 contributors.
The headline additions target everyday annoyances, including lazy imports via the lazy keyword, a first-class immutable frozendict, a real sentinel type, and UTF-8 as the default text encoding.
...
### Python 3.15.0 Ships With Lazy Imports, frozendict, and a Faster Interpreter
Python 3.15.0 is now available.
The core team at the Python Software Foundation confirmed the final build dropped on today, making it the latest major release in the language's history and the direct successor to 3.14.
...
The headline additions, like explicit lazy imports, a first-class immutable dictionary, a real sentinel type, and UTF-8 as the default text encoding, all chase the same petty daily frustrations.
Speed gains show up in a substantially beefed-up experimental JIT, a tail-calling interpreter for Windows, and free-threading turned on by default for macOS.
...
#### What actually changed
Development started May 7, 2025.
Alpha 1 landed in mid-October 2025, feature freeze hit at Beta 1 in May 2026, Candidate 3 on October 2, and the final build this week.
...
#### The speed stuff
Based on pyperformance numbers reported at doesjitgobrrr.com, you're looking at a 7 to 8 percent geometric mean improvement over stock CPython on x86-64 Linux, and 11 to 12 percent over the tail-calling interpreter on AArch64 macOS.

content.text: Python 3.15.0rc3, the final planned release candidate, shipped October 2 with about 156 fixes; last-minute lazy-import blockers delayed the final release, which is now scheduled for October 9, 2026.[1]
